pairs.q: Press Enter, the space bar, or tap this card.
pairs.a: There it is: the answer side. Press once more to go on.

pairs.q: Before you reveal a card, what do you do?
pairs.a: You answer first: in your head, out loud, or on paper. Then reveal.

pairs.q: You revealed the answer. What now?
pairs.a: Compare it with yours. Right? Good (Enter or space). Wrong? Again.

pairs.q: What happens when you tap Again?
pairs.a: The card comes back now, and once more later. Try it: tap Again, then Good next time.

pairs.q: Can a card have more than one side?
pairs.a: Yes. This one has two. Press on.

pairs.q: Second side. See the edge above the card?
pairs.a: That edge means: same word, going deeper. Up to ten sides.

pairs.q: What does the counter at the bottom count?
pairs.a: Cards you know. Ten make a deck. The deck is done when all ten are clean.

pairs.q: What happens when a deck is done?
pairs.a: Every word gets a score: +1 if clean, −1 or −2 if you slipped. The lowest come back first.

pairs.q: When does a word count as mastered?
pairs.a: At a score of 10. No streaks, no pressure: just your weakest words first.

pairs.q: How much better will you remember with WordDock?
pairs.a: A little. Say ten percent.

pairs.q: Then what is the ten percent for?
pairs.a: Reading and listening to the real language, with the words waiting in the back of your mind.

pairs.q: Why the name WordDock?
pairs.a: A word docks twice: in its context, and in the memory, the heart, of the one who learns it.

pairs.q: Where is the list behind this deck?
pairs.a: Tap the pale pill at the top: Studying 10 · WORDDOCK. A deck is a slice of a list.

pairs.q: What does the list show?
pairs.a: Every card as a row: question, answer, class, tags, level, and your score.

pairs.q: How do you find a word in the list?
pairs.a: Type it in the search box. Accents don't matter.

pairs.q: And all words of one class?
pairs.a: Tap the class in a row, say 'idea'. The list keeps only those.

pairs.q: What is the Level field for?
pairs.a: A band or a unit: A1, A1.2, or a range A1-A2. The list narrows to it.

pairs.q: Which words go into your next deck?
pairs.a: The ten weakest of what the list shows. Narrow the list, then tap Study.

pairs.q: Where are the other lists?
pairs.a: In the list, tap All lists at the top: published WD lists, and your own.

pairs.q: Can you study your own words?
pairs.a: Yes. Fill in an Excel sheet and add it under My Lists. The ? there has a template.

pairs.q: What does your own list need?
pairs.a: Only two columns: Q1 and A1. The file name becomes the list name.

pairs.q: Your scores live in this browser. How do you keep them safe?
pairs.a: Make a sync key, at the bottom of All lists. Enter it on another device: same progress.

pairs.q: Where is all this explained once more, in a few lines?
pairs.a: About WordDock, bottom right of All lists. Now tap WORDDOCK, then All lists, and pick a real list.
